blocks.text: Often called 'the forests of the sea', mangroves are salt-tolerant forests at the meeting of land and sea.

blocks.alt: A simple labelled landscape of a mangrove forest beside an information card.
blocks.caption: The mangrove forest: a labelled schematic and fact card (original diagram).
blocks.long_description: Mangrove trees with arching prop roots and upright breathing roots in shallow brackish water. The card gives the location (Indus delta at Keti Bandar and Mirpur Sakro, and the Balochistan coast), conditions (brackish water, oxygen-poor mud), plants (Avicennia marina, timmar, about 95% of the forest), animals (shrimps, crabs, mudskippers, turtles, dolphins, flamingo, crane, pelican) and status (threatened by less river water and pollution, helped by restoration).

blocks.caption: Profile of the mangrove forest
rows: Sindh (Keti Bandar and Mirpur Sakro in the Indus delta) and the Balochistan coast (Miani Hor, Kalmat Khor, Jiwani and Gawatar Bay)
brackish: fresh river water mixed with salty seawater
oxygen-poor mudflats; trees have breathing roots
Avicennia marina (timmar), about 95% of the forest
crocodiles, shrimps, mudskippers, crabs, lobsters, turtles, snakes, dolphins; flamingo, crane, pelican
threatened by less fresh water from the Indus and by pollution from Karachi; recent restoration projects have helped
